GD-013、GD-013 Ver.2.0 に続く 3 代目となるドライブペダルとなり、シリーズを引き継ぎつつ次世代機種としての意味を込め GD-XIIIと名付けられました。 ローゲインからハイゲインまで広範囲にカバーし、特にサウンドトラック制作に求められる幅広い世界観の構築に対応するべく開発されました。 初代、二代目と同じく、ゲーム・アニメ等の楽曲収録で絶大な人気を誇るギタリスト後藤貴徳氏、また GD-XIII ではゲームサウンドクリエイター・ギタリストの佐藤敦史氏も本格的に監修に加わり、両名による緻密で度重なるテストを経て完成しました。 回路は初代、二代目とは異なる新規の GD-XIII 回路となっており、根本的に新しいサウンドでありながら確実に GD-013 シリーズを踏襲したサウンドとなっています。 GD-013 シリーズのサウンドは既に世に出ている多くの作品の中で使用されており、そのサウンドは GD-XIII が次世代に引き継ぎます。 モデル名 : GD-XIII (ジーディーサーティーン) 種別 ： ディストーション 発売日 : 2023年 9月22日 価格 ：45,000円（税抜）/ 49,500円（税込） コントロール フットスイッチ オンオフスイッチです。オフ時はトゥルーパイパスです。 ノブ GAIN ゲイン量を調節します。 TONE 上げると高域が出ます。下げると高域が下がります。 LEVEL 出力音量を調節します。 トグルスイッチ 右トグルスイッチ（左右に動きます） High Gain Wide 広いレンジ感を保ったハイゲインモードです。基本のゲインが上がります。 Low Gain ローゲインモードです。基本のゲインが下がるとともに、重心が下がりしっかりとしたサウンドになります。ゲインを絞ってトーンを上げることでクランチサウンドを、ゲインを上げることで厚みのあるオーバードライブサウンドを得ることが出来ます。 High Gain 基本のゲインが上がります。High Gain Wideに比べてより中域に集中した密度の高いディストーションサウンドが得られます。 左トグルスイッチ（左右に動きます） Classic 歪み始めるポイントが早く、柔らかなアタックとより豊富な倍音が得られます。 Modern 歪み始めるポイントが遅く、アタックの芯が残り少し硬めのサウンドが得られます。 開発協力 ギタリスト 後藤貴徳 氏にはGD-013シリーズの1からご協力頂いており、主に直感的に気持ち良くプレーできるか、セッティングに手間取らずプレーに集中できるかという観点から監修頂きました。 ゲームサウンドクリエイター・ギタリスト 佐藤敦史 氏にはGD-013 ver2.0からご協力頂いており、主にアンサンブルの中でのEQバランスや、ラインやシミュレーター環境での相性、空間系との兼ね合いなどポストプロダクションの視点から監修頂きました。 ● 後藤貴徳氏 参加作品 ・NieR シリーズ ・エースコンバットシリーズ ・アイドルマスターシリーズ ・ラブライブ ・太鼓の達人 ・ウマ娘 ・ホロライブ ・仮面ライダーバトル ガンバレジェンズ ・アメージング The depth of sound has been increased to a finer gradation by upgrading the machined aluminum housing, parts, solder, etc. Specifications Weight: 450g Size: (W)950*95 x (D)113 x (H)54 (mm) Power source: 9V alkaline battery or pre-stabilized AC adapter, power supply (DC9V, center minus 2.1mm) This is an on/off switch. When off, it is a true bypass. Knobs,Toggle switches Knobs GAIN This is a gain adjustment, but up to about 12 o’clock, it is more like an EQ or EQ movement than a gain adjustment. In this range, it can be used in combination with the mode to actively create clean tones. After 12 o’clock, the gain and the push-out effect increases, so it can be used as a booster to adjust the push-out effect and texture of the boost, and as a stand-alone overdrive, it can be used like a gain knob. TONE When turned up, the high frequency range comes out. When turned down, it lowers the high frequency. LEVEL Adjusts the output volume; in NORMAL/BOLD , FLAT BOOST/MID BOOST mode, the output is higher than that of a normal effects pedal. Moderate settings are recommended to match the tolerances of the later stages. Right toggle switch (moves left and right) OVERDRIVE This gives a drive sound with an edge. By itself, it is suitable for creating sharp crunchy sounds. Boost mode is effective for creating a crunchy texture with fine overtones. Combined with the CLIPPED mode on the left toggle, you can get a sticky overdrive sound. FLAT BOOST This mode gives a flat boost feeling, and the more the GAIN is increased, the stronger the mid tone becomes. MID BOOST This mode provides more midrange boost and volume than the FLAT BOOST mode. Left toggle switch (moves left and right) CLIPPED This mode provides a strong sense of limit and soft distortion. sources.h1: Pettyjohn Electronics Edge Preamp & Low-Gain Overdrive
sources.description: Tone coneusseurs, rejoice! A new Pettyjohn Electronics pedal is here, it's called Edge, and it's a doozy!
sources.snippet: Pettyjohn Electronics Edge Preamp Low-Gain Overdrive
sources.bodyExcerpt: Pettyjohn Electronics Edge Preamp Low-Gain Overdrive | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Pettyjohn Electronics Edge Preamp & Low-Gain Overdrive Updated Mar. 26, 2021 | by Paolo De Gregorio Tone coneusseurs, rejoice! A new Pettyjohn Electronics pedal is here, it’s called Edge , and it’s a doozy! It’s a preamp pedal designed to deliver that magical blend of saturation, harmonic excitement, light compression you get from a tube amp at the edge of breakup. It can reach higher gain overdrive at higher settings, without ever squashing your tone thanks to its high overhead warranted by an internal circuit running at 18v. The dual-rail design shared by all the pedals in the company’s CORE series quadruples the headroom over standard 9v pedals. Another nice touch: the blue LED lights up when the circuit is driven past the edge of breakup, giving a real-time visual of how the circuit is overloading. On top of that, the company offers two Custom Mod Upgrades on the standard model: An Orange LED for slightly lower headroom and more overdrive, and a Yellow Mod for even lower headroom but tighter low-end and slightly more breakup and chimey harmonic overtones. Hear the Pettyjohn Electronics Edge in the videos below. There is a sweet spot on almost every tube amp or overdrive pedal most guitarists know well. A magical zone where the circuit goes non-linear and starts to saturate. Harmonics excited by this process make everything sound alive giving the player a unique interactive experience with great tough-sensitive dynamics. The EDGE is a pedal specially designed to explore the sonic magic that happens when a circuit is pushed to the edge of breakup. The EDGE is voiced to give a rich blend of saturation, harmonic excitement, light compression and then, at max gain, start to fully breakup. At lower gains, sweet clean tones are easy to come by, in the spirit of several popular vintage preamps, and could easily be used as a slightly colored clean boost. The EDGE has been designed to give a slight bit of vintage character while offering advantages of modern components and design, such as high headroom dual rail power supply (up to 36v of voltage swing!) and musical, sweepable 18 db/octave filters. What makes the EDGE’s wide sweet spot possible is a set of carefully curated clipping LED’s, specifically chosen for their smooth clipping characteristics and wide saturation curve. The LED’s light up when driven past the edge of breakup and this give us the opportunity to have a real-time visual of how the circuit is overloading. We made this LED visible on top of the pedal, effectively functioning as a visual threshold light for the EDGE of breakup. CORE Series Simplicity The CORE Series features a streamlined control set for quickly dialing in killer tones with four knobs to adjust Level, Gain, Lows and Highs. CORE Series Dual Rail Power We designed the CORE Series with a dual rail doubling power supply. This design can scale from +/-7v to +/-18v, effecting the headroom, tone and feel of the pedal, achieving up to four times the headroom over standard 9v pedals. The internal supply achieves this by mirroring whatever input voltage you apply via the external power supply and we always encourage people to experiment. CORE Series Quiet Bypass Our entire CORE Series features our quiet bypass switching system. It is a true bypass, relay based system for minimum pop when engaging the effect. sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - Stephen Pettyjohn Explores the outer reaches of Headroom and Compression with his Elegant New Chime-derived Core Edge Circuit ao link News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Xploration • Curation • Recommendation News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Filter content by area of interest Amps Boost and Overdrive Delay Distortion Fuzz Guitars Modulation Pitch Reverb Utility All All Stephen Pettyjohn Explores the outer reaches of Headroom and Compression with his Elegant New Chime-derived Core Edge Circuit Apr 1, 2021 18:05 by Stefan Karlsson Boost Boost and Overdrive Overdrive Pettyjohn Electronics Vox Style Distortion + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points Pettyjohn Electronics' Core Edge Low Gain Overdrive (Gørva-enclosured) extends the Chime Overdrive. LED options: Blue (max headroom, gentle bloom), Orange and Yellow (quicker breakup). Edge controls: Level, Drive, Lows, Highs. Chime controls: Level, Variable Clipping Diodes (Ge>LED), Drive, Tilt EQ, HPF 700Hz–30kHz, Boost. Chime with NOS Telefunken AA132 Germanium Diodes. Edge: low‑gain soft bloom. Chime: top‑boosted Vox/Brian May tones. They stack with JA Bloom and ThorpyFX Heavy Water. Available on Pettyjohn Electronics Web Store; Blue Edge appears at dealers within the next week or two. Plans: Iron MKII and Gold MKII; consult a qualified tech before opening or modifying pedals. The latest Pettyjohn Electronics Pedal is the Core Edge Low Gain Overdrive (Gørva-enclosured). This pedal owes its pedigree to Pettyjohn’s best-selling Chime Overdrive - which per the visual can really be considered the sort of Senior version of that circuit. Obviously we have slightly different controls, and at default the Chime is loaded with Yellow LEDs - which are designed for relatively quick-onset breakup. While the default Edge comes with Blue LEDs designed for maximum low gain prowess, and ultimate headroom. You can select for your Edge to have either Orange or original Chime Yellow LED’s in place of the Blue - which get progressively quicker on the breakup - thus descending in Headroom - it really depends on what you’re after here. As mentioned in the title, the Edge pedal is also an exploration into the fairly subtle onset of compression and how that colours and texturizes the tone - and where you will get slightly different results with the different types of LEDs. I think it would have been cool here to have had socketed slots on the board for easy switching of LEDs, or even better still - some sort of 3-way switch with all options onboard. I would have 3 LEDs visible then - so you can see the bloom of the gain for each option. The cool thing about the circuit is that you get dynamic feedback on what is happening via one of the actual active LEDs appearing at the centre of the pedal. Possibly these enhanced extrapolations are something for the future. The Chime has really clever controls - L

Pettyjohn Electronics browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Pettyjohn Electronics RAIL - Fuzz Published on November 18, 2023 Pettyjohn Electronics fuzz pedal Information Pettyjohn Electronics The RAIL is a full-range fuzz machine with something for everyone. RAIL boasts a simple but powerful set of controls allowing for a vast range of fuzzed out and distorted tones. The RAIL features a simple but powerful four-knob control set: Level, Gain, Lows, and Highs. Explore each in detail below along with our Pettyjohn Custom Shop options only available from Pettyjohn online. Product Description The first pedal in the new Pettyjohn Electronics CORE Series, the RAIL is a true full-range fuzz machine! In traditional Pettyjohn fashion, we have brought rigorous engineering, creative design and a passion for tone shaping to craft a versatile fuzz for everyone at unmatched value. Explore all that RAIL has to offer below. GAIN The GAIN is set by a unique eight-position rotary switch and provides an inordinate amount of tone shaping while being intuitive to use. This is due to the rotary switch providing an increased range of gain which can not be found in standard pots. With this extra gain the RAIL provides significantly improved processing on the high levels at each increment of gain. Step your way from low gain distortion (which cleans up nicely) all the way up to Infinity mode. Infinity mode simulates infinite gain and is by far the craziest fuzz setting we have ever engineered, complete with a light musical gating effect. The RAIL circuit takes a unique approach to generating fuzz which does not rely on clipping diodes or finicky vintage transistors. Instead, the pedal literally boosts the signal with extreme levels of gain into the voltage rails and hence the orgin of the name "RAIL". This effect is made even more fun thanks to our dual power rail design, which can scale from +/-6v to +/-18v, with the internal supply mirroring whatever input voltage you apply via the external power supply. Lower the voltage, lower the headroom and increase the clipping amount. There is a sweet spot for everyone, so experiment to find your perfect fuzz tone. Hosted in a beautiful, black, blunt compact case, this pedal is a full range fuzz and the first release in the builder’s new Core Series. Ideal for heavy riffing, at lower levels, the Rail can deliver more subtle overdriven tones, while it can sound like a gated fuzz when the gain is pushed to the max. The Drive knob has 8 positions pushing different amounts of gain. The Low control is placed before the fuzz, while the highs knobs is placed post-gain to highlight or tame the fizziness. sources.bodyExcerpt: Pettyjohn Rous Distortion | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Pettyjohn Rous Distortion Updated Oct. 26, 2020 | by Paolo De Gregorio The RAT Distortion belongs to that very exclusive pedal circuit “elite” that provides seemingly infinite inspiration to stompbox builders. We know something about it, since we’ve been working for over a year on a comprehensive article about RAT clones, and each and every time we try to finalize it we are overwhelmed by the sheer size of models on the market. Oregon’s boutique builder Pettyjohn Electronics has built a solid reputation in the dirt box arena, and a RAT-style pedal was missing from their roster: enter the ROUS . The references to the RAT aren’t disguised – ROUS stands for “Rodent of Unusual Size” – but, of course, this is far from a simple recreation. Here are the main differences from the original: The Pettyjohn ROUS runs at 7-18v , which allows for an extended gain range and, at higher voltage, adds headroom and dynamics It features two EQ knobs (pre-gain Lows and post-gain Highs ) instead of one, for more precise tone sculpting. A Fire/Swamp toggle switch delivers two different style of distortion: Fire delivers silicon hard clipping that more closely resembles the aggressive tone of the original unit, while the Swamp mode adds a Germanium diode into the equation, delivering softer clipping with vintage overtones, making it perfect for less aggressive genres like country, blues and pop. Here are the latest videos of the Pettyjohn Rous Distortion. You can find other similar pedals in our Rat-Style Distortion Pedal coverage. The ROUS, “Rodent of Unusual Size”, is a highly evolved member of the RAT family. The ROUS features a simple but powerful four knob control set: Level, Gain, Lows and Highs, similar to the other CORE series pedals. Its gain range moves from low gain overdrive to unusually large sounding distorted tones quickly with the turn of the GAIN knob. One may take matters of fate into their own hands and journey deeper into the un-known with a flick of the Fire Swamp switch. Explore the feature set in detail below and for those looking to choose their own adventure, you can discover more paths to sonic nirvana with custom mod options only available from the Pettyjohn online shop. sources.bodyExcerpt: Testimonials - Phaez Amplification Skip to content Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button Main Menu Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button This is just a small sampling of customer comments. This is for the M800+, 4XEL84 version Aug 2026 “Good morning Randy, I got the amp yesterday, and spent yesterday afternoon and evening playing. I have to be honest with you, it is the most amazing sounding amp I have ever owned in my 59 years, and I’ve owned quite a few. Over the years. A Marshall 2204, JCM800, Rick Onslow Super Bass, Silver Jubilee , Voodoo VRock, Mesa Mark3. Carvin Legacy. I’m really blown away by how great it sounds, and your McBoosty works great with it too, as well as the Daisy Cutter. ” “ Hi Randy, just a quick hello from Montreal. I’m loving this amp. It sounds like hit records! It does Van Halen, Slash, Steve Vai, Neil Schon, name it. Just fabulous! I’ve never had a Marshall that could do that. It just puts a smile on my face every time I plug into it” About an 18W Daisycutter: “Hi Randy, I picked up what appears to be an older 18w EL84 Daisycutter and wanted to drop in some new power tubes since the history of the current JJs is unknown. Does the Daisycutter run a fixed bias? Anything to consider when swapping in a new set? By the way the amp is just SO good! I own a Suhr SL67 and a 50w Bogner Helios and this little beast goes toe to toe with them! Killer tones!! “ Double M (40W Plexi channel and J+ channel) “Just wanted to check in: I’ve been playing the amp every day and each time I’m completely impressed. The depth control is a little different from the amps I’ve played in the past (mainly Peavey Ultra and 5150, and some tube Randalls). I’ve had it set to noon and to my ears it sounds like it adds a cleaner signal ontop of the dirty signal. Granted, that’s with ear-plugs in through a 4×12. Completely impressed “ Double M (40W Plexi + Boosted JCM) “Hi Randy, Just want to thank you again for the fantastic work. I’m a big metal guy but seem to be playing more the Plexi side than the JCM side. Great for stuff like the Stones and AC/DC with a little punch from a tube screamer…so damm great. And with the JCM side there I get my metal with a little modulation in the effects loop and blues driver or OD-1 in the front for that solo push. Just a well thought out and executed amp. Cheers! “ 18W Daisycutter: “I’ve rehearsed and gigged with the amp now, and I’m SHOCKED. I’m playing classic rock, modern rock, dance/funk, 90’s alternative, and even some modern pop and it’s just killer. Super responsive to my volume knob for cleanish to heavy grind and it takes pedals in front of the amp and in the loop like a champ.. I’ve paired it with a Friedman 1×12 ported cab with a Scumback BM75 (a 70’s blackback and it’s just crazy good modded Marshall tones all day. I was always concerned that going to a small, EL84 amp meant sacrificing tone and feel compared to my “big” amps, but mic’d up thru my in-ears it’s amazing. Those now stay at home and I use my mini-rig for everything. It’s cut down on the load in/out hassle factor for sure! “ This comment from the owner the Cheyenne, a 4XEL84 Matchless type channel switcher “ We have it outside with a full band tonight. You absolutely nailed it. This thing is unreal “ McClane owner “Ive got a McClane. It’s the best amp ever. It can hang with much more expensive amps. Also even at 15w it can punch through with a pretty loud band” This comment about a 25W Barracuda (channel switcher) with one channel a Corona/Fender BF Twin, and the other channel mid gain Marshall (my design tweaked over many many years) “Hey Randy! Finally got to crank this amp up nice and loud and wanted to say wow. Sounds great! The Fender side breaks up nicely and the Marshall side drives like a teen at the wheel! I appreciate it. One of

sources.bodyExcerpt: Previous Builds Page 6 - Phaez Amplification Skip to content Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button Main Menu Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button Page 1 Page 2 Page 3 Page 4 Page 5 Page 6 Daisycutter Dual This 35W Daisycutter Dual is somewhat related to the Atticus but it has separate inputs vs channel switching. Sourmash head cab. There are a pair of EL34’s in the output stage and are run conservatively which leads to a long, long life. H channel is my high gain 4 stage OD Daisycutter channel, related to the Asheville but does not use a cold clipper. The L channel is my Corona (Blackface/Twin). It has a loop with a level that will not overdrive 9V pedals. Sluggo 50 Sluggo is a 50 watt EL34 amp and is somewhat related to the Atticus. A channel switcher and relays are not in the signal path when the channel is selected. Was a custom build. The H channel is my high gain 4 stage OD Daisycutter channel, related to the Asheville but does not use a cold clipper. The L channel is my Corona (Blackface/Twin). It has a loop with a level that will not overdrive 9V pedals. Continuum A custom build with a 2 Rock John Mayer as the basis. An amp more in the clean territory and has a loop. Pair of 6L6’s in the output section for about 35W. Customer was sourcing his own head cab. I don’t really like the hanging orientation as heat can build up. Variable negative feedback. Dirty Jackpot Another custom build, the Dirty Jackpot is really very impressive! Output tubes are a pair of EL84’s connected in TRIODE and results in about 7W output. This has a footswitchable boost and the core of the circuit is my AFD which is a high gain hot rodded M style circuit (it is superb!). Proper heater voltage, proper loop level. Pasadena 50W EVH’s hometown. This is one of the Pasadena’s I did with EL34’s. Has a loop. It sounds better and is more versatile than the Friedman Custom Small Box it is sitting on. I know the Friedman circuit well, not anything earth-shattering. Kodiak 4 x KT88 This thing is big and heavy lol. 4 x KT88 in output section. DNA is from an Orange AD200 Jackpot 7W A custom build and another example of triode connected EL84’s, resulting in about 7 watts. 2 channel, separate inputs. The Z input is a Z-wreck/AC30 input and the R input in my Riggs circuit which is a slightly modified Corona. There is a loop on this one too. Jomama Another custom build and related to the Atticus. A 35W channel switcher. There is a pair of EL34’s in the output stage and are run very conservatively so they should last for many years. OD high gain channel and pristine clean channel (F-based). Bluesbender The Bluesbender was a custom build and is essentially a Pasadena but with a JTM/Bassman type tonestack. 18W from a pair of EL84’s. Proper amount of feedback applied. No loop on this one. JT Special A custom build. This is a 50 watt EL34 amp and is essentially a Pasadena. This one has footswitchable boost – it is adjustable and there is an LED on when it is engaged. Yes, it has a loop too. I have the word “SUPERB” written in large letters on the schematic. Eruption Here is another custom build and the customer was sourcing the head cab. This is a single-ended amp with an EL34 in the output section and is about 11W power output. Main circuit is the Pasadena (hometown of EVH) and this amp also has a loop. Galamad 33 The Galamad was a custom build and is somewhat related to the Atticus. It has separate inputs vs channel switching. Customer was sourcing the head cab. There are a pair of 6L6’s in the output stage and are run conservatively which leads to a long long life. H channel is my high gain 4 stage OD channel, related to the Asheville but does not use a cold clipper. The L channel is my Corona (Blackface/Twin). sources.title: Here is a clip of the Phaez Iron Viper pedal into the EL34 Blackwater amp. The Iron Viper is a distortion pedal with a really nice chewy tone, the amp is wonderful clean machine, and the two complement each other wonderfully. The iphone has compression in the software what makes seem my speaking voice is as a loud as the amp but that ain't the case. Was loud but not obscenely so. I mention at the end the video that I will be including an Iron Viper pedal with the purchase of the EL34 Blackwater. Check my website. Cheers! | Phaez Amplification

sources.bodyExcerpt: PEDALS - Phaez Amplification Skip to content Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button Main Menu Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button A WHOLE LOTTA PEDAL STUFF Well folks I have been spending a LOT of time analyzing, designing, and building pedals. This are will get filled up shortly. But here is the tentative plan – I will offering twists on some great pedals. I will fully explain why I made certain small changes and it going to be A WHOLE LOTTA FUN. What is critical about pedal use is the other half of the equation. THE AMP. You need a good pedal friendly amp! If not, you are wasting your time IMO. More on this later. As pedals become available for sale you should see them pop up here. But keep in mind I am not planning a mass production type offering – each pedal will be INDIVIDUAL . I am going to giving you the opportunity to have a custom name and colour for your pedal and the overall design of the pedal will follow some basic structures. I don’t foresee any tubescreamer type pedals in the future offerings as there are already a million different versions out there, but who knows? My pedals are designed to run on a regular 9V pedal power supply – no battery option. If battery powered is something you need, let me know. Pedals are all handmade by yours truly, so no fancy box or details instructions. PRICES INCLUDE SHIPPING 2026 LINEUP: M Class Distortion Alligator Overdrive McBoosty Emperor Distortion (M Guv) NEW FOR July 2026. The Alligator overdrive. Fantastic tonal control via a Fender Twin/Blackface tonestack. Works fantastic into a Marshall style amp. BUY THIS PEDAL US$99 Emperor - the respected Marshall Guv'nor circuit, but this one, unlike the Marshall, is reliable. A GREAT distortion pedal. The GUV is the choice of the great Gary Moore. ON SALE. BUY THIS PEDAL US$89 M-Class addresses 2 small points in the Guv'nor. YES it is an improvement. More output and ACTUAL Marshall JCM/Plexi tonestack, Ship incl. SIDE JACKS. ON SALE. BUY THIS PEDAL US$89 I think the M-Class is the REFERENCE STANDARD in distortion pedals M-Class addresses 2 small points in the Guv'nor. YES it is an improvement. More output and ACTUAL Marshall JCM/Plexi tonestack, Ship incl. SIDE JACKS. ON SALE. BUY THIS PEDAL US$89 I think the M-Class is the REFERENCE STANDARD in distortion pedals The M-Class addresses 2 small points in the Guv'nor. YES it is an improvement. More output and ACTUAL Marshall JCM/Plexi tonestack, Ship incl. TOP JACKS SOLD! M-Class was formerly known as the Emperor+ McBoosty boost pedal. You may never want to turn it off. Clean/OD knob goes from clean to OD (duh) Very useful tone control THIS IS A UNIQUE PEDAL, IT DOES NOT REPLICATE ANYTHING YOU CURRENTLY HAVE BUY THIS PEDAL CDN$129 Octopus - my take of the Fulltone OCD circuit SOLD! Daisycutter - a great 4 knob distortion pedal. Lots of tweak SOLD! Savage - lotsa gain, my take on the RAT, more versatile SOLD! Iron Viper - based on the BJFe Dyna Red Distortion SOLD! Clicking on the pics will enlarge If you don't mind waiting you can have your choice of faceplate colour, enclosure colour, and maybe even a custom name. Contact me for more info. PROCO RAT PHAEZ SAVAGE CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFO Solar Chug Pedal (excellent) retail is US$199.00 Contact me! KSR Ceres Pedal (excellent) retail is US$399.99 Contact me! BJF Dyna Red Distortion I also want to mention the BJFe Dyna Red Distortion. It’s been around for a long time and is loved by many. This is not just another distortion pedal – this thing has some great FUZZ going on with the gain up. It’s really a cool tone. Red LED’s in the feedback loop – NICE. I have got to the heart of what makes the Dyna Red tick, and have come up with the Iron Viper. One thing I don’t really like about the original is the unity gain buffer at the end of the circuit which follows a couple of diodes which really clamp the voltage. This has been a minor complaint of the Dyna Red Distortion

sources.bodyExcerpt: Savage Pedal - Phaez Amplification Skip to content Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button Main Menu Home PEDALS About Search for: Search Button The Proco Rat is a classic for a reason There are millions of Proco Rat pedals out there. The pedal has been out since 1978 has there have some changes here and there. The early ones used the LM308 chip and then later switched to the OP07DP. But what is the main factor in the sound of Rat? It is not the slew rate of the LM308 – yeah that causes some HF rolloff but there are ways to mimic that. And no it is not the chip clipping. Clipping infers that the device has reached saturation and cannot deliver the current in a linear fashion. But what is really going on is the opamp is HITTING THE RAILS. THE PS RAILS. Look, the max gain of the Rat circuit is a whopping 2300X. Yes that’s right, whatever the output of your pickups is supposed to get amplified 2300X (if you are plugging directly in). And a high output humbucker can hit 1 volt p-p. That means in a perfect circuit, the output would be 2300V. Needless to say, it doesn’t. In fact, the signal starts hitting the rails pretty early on with respect the gain pot position. It hits the rails because of the limits of the 9VDC power supply. That is the first issue for me. The clipping you hear is the signal hitting the rails, not the diode clipping, which follows right after the opamp. Not that it sounds bad, but that fact is almost 100% overlooked, and even the designers (copiers?) of all the Rat style pedals out there don’t recognize it. Those subsequent diodes can’t really square off an already squared off signal. And the diode options some pedals have? If those diodes have a larger forward voltage (like a red LED) then the pedal is just louder, but the squareness of the signal is still the same. And the no-diode option? Again the result is the pedal just being louder and the distortion you hear is the signal hitting the PS rail. Issue #2 for me, and don’t misunderstand me, none of these are fatal flaws, just places where the Rat could be improved. But #2 is the too simple tone control. It is 6db per octave filter and the result is a sloped response through out the treble region. I would prefer a shelved response (that what I have done with the Savage.) Issue #3 is it’s low output. Don’t you want to hit your amp a bit harder. Almost always sounds better IMO. With the stock diodes in the Rat pedal you end up with what I consider to be miniscule output. Issue #4 is the use of cheap electrolytic coupling caps. C’mon there are better options than that! Issue #5 is the limited ability to shape the tone – but that is something that affects MANY pedals. But I have addressed that in the Savage, making it much more versatile. So what is the Savage? Well the DNA is all RAT but me addressing the issues I have raised earlier. I have come with a very very cool dual gain system, and each does tone shaping at the same time. Gain 1 pulls some treble as you turn it up (yes that is desirable) and Gain 2 adds some low end when you dial it back. When Gain 2 is dimed – you are in original RAT territory, but as I mentioned early the original Rat has oodles of gain, 2300X!! You can get a much nicer crunch and almost bouncy mid gain tones with that Gain 2 option. So the Gain controls offer a nice way to shape the tone, in addition to the tone control. My tone control, is better than the stock one. The stock one is a TILT throughout, the Savage offers more of a shelf response. I don’t use any electrolytics in the signal path. I have a RECOVERY stage which provides a much higher output than the original. I have an aversion to low output pedals. I found the BEST SOUNDING opamp for this circuit. The TLC072CP, no not the TL072CP but the TLC072CP, the expensive big brother. So that is a summary of the Savage pedal. I will be updating this description but if you want one hit the BUY IT NOW! SAVA

sources.title: Pigtronix Gamma Drive Overdrive Pedal | Harmonic Clipping — Pursell Lutherie
sources.description: Unleash touch-sensitive distortion with the Pigtronix Gamma Drive. Features a unique blend of Germanium, LED, and Silicon diodes with an active Baxandall EQ.
sources.snippet: Pigtronix Gamma Drive Overdrive Pedal | Harmonic Clipping — Pursell ...
sources.bodyExcerpt: Pigtronix Gamma Drive Overdrive Pedal | Harmonic Clipping — Pursell Lutherie Skip to Content Open Menu Close Menu About Events Music Lessons Repair Gallery Marketplace Contact Us Pursell Lutherie 0 0 Open Menu Close Menu About Events Music Lessons Repair Gallery Marketplace Contact Us Pursell Lutherie 0 0 About Events Music Lessons Repair Gallery Marketplace Contact Us Shop the Collection › Pigtronix Gamma Drive Image 1 of 3 Image 2 of 3 Image 3 of 3 Pigtronix Gamma Drive $129.00 Pedal Type: Asymmetrical Harmonic Overdrive Controls: Volume, Gain, Treble, and Bass Knobs Bypass Layout: True Bypass Switching Power Requirements: 9VDC Negative Center (Can accept up to 18VDC for increased headroom) Current Draw: 100 mA Dimensions: 1.5” × 3.75” × 1.75” (38.1 mm x 95.2 mm x 44.4 mm) Asymmetrical Diode Blending and Rich Harmonic Saturation Multi-Material Clipping Architecture for Amp-Like Response The Pigtronix Gamma Drive redefines standard overdrive design by stepping away from traditional single-flavor clipping structures. The entirely analog signal path implements a specialized, interactive matrix pairing Germanium, Silicon, and LED diodes arranged specifically to achieve asymmetrical clipping. By combining these distinct clipping elements, the pedal mimics the complex, touch-sensitive breakup characteristics of a tube amplifier pushing into natural saturation. This custom hardware engineering yields prominent second-order harmonics, keeping complex note arrangements sweet, smooth, and defined even under heavy clipping. Active 2-Band EQ Tuning and Frequency Optimization Unlike standard drive pedals that utilize passive tone controls to merely shave off treble response, this micro-enclosure houses a sophisticated active EQ section. The Treble control manages a shelving filter centered at 2kHz, while the Bass control features a shelving network tuned at 80Hz. Both bands offer up to 12dB of precise octave cut or boost, allowing the player to sculpt their instrument's footprint or adapt to different venue acoustics seamlessly. Leaving the dials in their detented center positions delivers a perfectly flat frequency response across the global gain structure. Creative Rig Integration and Circuit Optimization High-Definition Harmonic Clean Boosting Setting the master Gain control completely counterclockwise configures the internal active circuitry as a pristine, low-impedance line booster. Cranking the master Volume pot delivers an immense output surge to push tube preamps into overdrive, while the active Treble and Bass controls allow you to fine-tune the signal's frequency boundaries to perfectly match single-coil or humbucker configurations. Compressed Fluid Lead Voicing with High Voltage Headroom Running the device at its full 18VDC capability expands internal headroom, providing enhanced dynamic picking response and a massive output ceiling. Dialing the Gain knob past noon yields a singing, highly compressed hard rock sustain that tracks your touch flawlessly. This application excels at delivering articulate, fluid solo tones that sit directly on top of heavy rhythm tracks without turning brittle or washed out. THIS PEDAL REQUIRES A STANDARD 9V DC CENTER NEGATIVE POWER SUPPLY AND CONSUMES 100MA. IT DOES NOT OPERATE WITH BATTERIES. DO NOT EXCEED 18V DC, AS HIGHER VOLTAGES WILL VOID YOUR WARRANTY AND CAUSE PERMANENT COMPONENT DAMAGE. Add To Cart Added! sources.bodyExcerpt: Pigtronix Gas Giant Fuzz | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Pigtronix Gas Giant Fuzz Updated Jul. 23, 2025 | by Paolo De Gregorio Inspired by the early Muffs, the Pigtronix Gas Giant is a high-gain analog jumbo fuzz pedal that delivers monstrous tones with modern precision, using quad-matched transistor sets to lock in that elusive “sweet spot” found in those classic circuits from the ’70s—only with far more consistency and reliability. At its core, the Gas Giant packs a powerful trio of controls: Gain, Volume, and a dual-voice Tone knob thanks to the Bump/Scoop switch , alternatively delivering a thunderous low-end, scooped mids, and searing highs, or Pigtronix’s signature mid-forward “Bump” setting for cutting through dense mixes. This versatility ensures everything from doom-laden sludge to articulate, snarling leads. To tame the inherent noise of extreme fuzz, the Gas Giant includes a switchable noise gate with high-speed FET circuitry—borrowed from Pigtronix’s Gatekeeper and fine-tuned for this pedal. It effortlessly silences unwanted hiss without compromising dynamics, adapting seamlessly to any pickup type. Built for practicality, the Gas Giant features true bypass switching, runs on standard 9VDC power (under 100mA), and sports a compact, pedalboard-friendly design. sources.bodyExcerpt: Pigtronix Gas Giant Fuzz Review (2025): Thick, Creamy, Cosmic Fuzz in a Compact Stompbox - Tone Authority – Guitar Bass Gear Reviews Skip to content Tone Authority – Guitar Bass Gear Reviews Blog Contact FAQ About Pigtronix Gas Giant Fuzz Review (2025): Thick, Creamy, Cosmic Fuzz in a Compact Stompbox June 18, 2025 Fuzz That Cuts, Creams, and Crushes Blast off into vintage fuzz heaven — without losing your mids in the black hole. The Pigtronix Gas Giant Fuzz is a compact, no-nonsense analog fuzz pedal that delivers rich midrange , big sustain , and earth-shaking character — all while remaining remarkably controllable and musical . It’s perfect for players who love vintage fuzz but want something that sits better in a modern mix , responds to dynamics , and doesn’t turn to mush on stage. Affiliate Disclosure: This article contains affiliate links. We may earn a small commission if you purchase through them — at no extra cost to you. It helps keep the riffs loud and the reviews honest. 🔥 Why the Gas Giant Stands Out Feature Why It Matters All-analog circuit Vintage tone with modern reliability Midrange-focused voice Cuts through the mix Sustain and Tone knobs Dial in thick, violin-like sustain or tight fuzz grit Compact enclosure Pedalboard-friendly and built like a tank Made in the USA Boutique tone without boutique price tag 🎧 What It Sounds Like: Imagine a Big Muff and a Tone Bender got in a bar fight — and both came out better. The Gas Giant delivers: 🌋 Creamy, warm sustain — like a fuzz-soaked lead tone from a classic rock record 🧱 Tight, focused lows — doesn’t get flubby or overpowering 🌌 Harmonic richness — reacts beautifully to tube amps and drive pedals ⚡ Touch dynamics — cleans up well with your guitar volume knob This is not a one-trick fuzz. It excels at both stoner rock riffing and violin-like lead tones , making it a serious weapon for both rhythm and lead players. 🎛️ Controls Breakdown Volume – Loud enough to push your amp Tone – Sweepable EQ with a wide range, especially effective in mids Gain – Adjusts fuzz intensity without getting harsh 💡 Unlike many fuzzes, the tone knob here doesn’t scoop your sound into oblivion. 🎸 Perfect For Players Who Want: ✅ Vintage fuzz character with a modern, gig-ready voicing ✅ Lead guitar tones that sing, not splatter ✅ A fuzz pedal that cuts through the mix instead of vanishing in it ✅ A fuzz that plays nice with overdrive, delay, or modulation pedals ✅ A high-quality boutique pedal that won’t eat your board space or budget 🔊 Genre Matchmaking 🎸 Stoner Rock / Doom – Pair with a tube amp for mammoth riff tone 🔥 Classic Rock – Violin lead tones and Page-style fuzz 💀 Garage / Punk – Raw, aggressive fuzz with just enough control 🌀 Shoegaze / Alt – Stacks beautifully with modulation and delay 🎛️ Synth or Bass? – Surprisingly solid low-end handling on bass too 🧪 Build Quality Design Rugged die-cast chassis True bypass switching Top-mounted jacks for tight pedalboard fit Hand-assembled in the USA It’s built for stage abuse but refined enough for studio work. 💰 Price Value At around $130–$150 , the Pigtronix Gas Giant delivers boutique fuzz tone without the usual boutique markup. It easily competes with — and in some cases outperforms — much pricier fuzzes in its class. 👉 Shop at zZounds 🏁 Final Thoughts: The Pigtronix Gas Giant Fuzz is the fuzz pedal for players who want more than just chaos . It’s tight, musical, thick, and expressive — a pedal that takes your tone to space but still lands every note. If you’re tired of fuzzes that either disappear or overwhelm your mix, the Gas Giant strikes the perfect balance. It’s big, bold, and beautiful — and absolutely ready for liftoff. sources.bodyExcerpt: Philosopher's Gold by Pigtronix | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Pigtronix Philosopher's Gold LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS COMPRESSOR SUSTAINER Description Philosopher’s Gold is a variation on the original Philosopher’s Tone, featuring the same optical sustain engine with the addition of an optional layer of germanium-enhanced distortion. The unique diode arrangement found in the Philosopher’s Gold delivers a smooth top end and rich midrange response, tailored to match the characteristics of the optical sustainer driving it. The clean side of the Philosopher’s Tone remains the same—dial in your Blend and Volume to get your desired signal, and Sustain for compression. What defines Germanium Gold is the Grit control. More than a simple gain knob, Grit acts as a blend for the supreme germanium-enhanced distortion folded into the unit. sources.snippet: Pigtronix Philosopher's Gold Pedal - Guitar.com
sources.bodyExcerpt: Pigtronix Philosopher's Gold Pedal | Guitar.com News Reviews Guides Features Magazine Tuner Deals Pigtronix Pigtronix Philosopher's Gold Pedal This compressor and germanium distortion pedal combines an optical sustain engine with germanium-enhanced distortion. It features Volume, Sustain, Grit, and Blend controls, allowing precise adjustment of compression and overdrive. The Grit control blends in the germanium overdrive stage, adding rich midrange response. The pedal includes the same optical compression as the original Philosopher's Tone, tailored for dynamic sustain and distortion. sources.h1: Pigtronix Star Eater Review: Is This Analog Delay + Reverb Pedal Worth It?
sources.description: A detailed, musician-first review of the Pigtronix Star Eater — covering sound quality, build, real-world use, and how it compares to alternatives like the Boss RV-6 and Strymon Blue Sky.
sources.snippet: Pigtronix Star Eater Review: Is This Analog Delay + Reverb Pedal Worth ...
sources.bodyExcerpt: Pigtronix Star Eater Review: Is This Analog Delay + Reverb Pedal Worth It? | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Pigtronix Star Eater Review: Is This Analog Delay + Reverb Pedal Worth It? By liam-carter June 6, 2026 Pigtronix Star Eater Review: A Deep Dive Into Its Analog Delay + Reverb Capabilities The Pigtronix Star Eater is a dual-engine analog delay and reverb pedal designed for players seeking organic texture, dynamic response, and hands-on control—not presets or digital sterility. It occupies a distinct niche between boutique analog delay units (like the Malekko Chaoscillator) and hybrid digital reverbs (such as the Strymon Blue Sky), prioritizing circuit-level authenticity over feature count. For guitarists, bassists, and keyboard players who value modulation-rich analog delay tails paired with spring- and plate-style reverb tones—and who don’t need MIDI, looping, or stereo I/O—the Star Eater delivers compelling sonic character and tactile immediacy. However, its fixed 120ms max delay time, lack of tap tempo subdivision options, and mono-only signal path limit its utility in complex rhythmic contexts or modern production workflows. If you’re asking ‘Is the Pigtronix Star Eater worth buying for expressive, vintage-leaning ambient textures?’ , the answer is yes—provided your musical priorities align with its focused, no-compromise analog philosophy. About Pigtronix Star Eater: Product Background and Intent Pigtronix, founded in 2004 by electrical engineer and musician Brian D’Addario, has built a reputation on high-fidelity analog circuit design, rigorous component selection, and rejection of digital convenience where it compromises tone. The Star Eater debuted in 2017 as part of Pigtronix’s ‘Eater’ series—preceded by the Philosopher’s Tone (compressor) and followed by the Keymaster (octave generator). Unlike most multi-effect pedals, the Star Eater does not attempt to emulate digital reverb algorithms or offer dozens of delay modes. Instead, it combines two discrete, hand-tuned analog circuits: a bucket-brigade device (BBD) delay line using the MN3207 chip, and an all-analog reverb tank simulation built around discrete op-amps and passive networks. Its goal is singular: to generate warm, decaying, harmonically rich repeats and resonant, non-linear reverb decay that behaves like physical springs or plates—not mathematically perfect impulse responses. This philosophy reflects Pigtronix’s broader stance: tone is shaped by voltage behavior, capacitor tolerances, and thermal drift—not just sample rates and DSP headroom. First Impressions: Build Quality, Setup, and Design Unboxing reveals a compact 4.5" × 3.75" × 2" enclosure milled from 16-gauge steel—substantially heavier than similarly sized pedals (1.2 lbs / 544 g). The brushed black powder-coated finish resists scuffs, and all controls are recessed C&K tactile switches or smooth, detented Alps potentiometers with knurled aluminum shafts. There are no LEDs on the faceplate—only illuminated status rings around each knob (green for delay, blue for reverb)—a deliberate choice to reduce visual distraction and eliminate LED-related noise coupling. Power input accepts only 9–12 V DC center-negative (no battery option); Pigtronix specifies a regulated supply delivering ≥250 mA. Initial setup requires no firmware updates, calibration, or app pairing—just plug in instrument and amp. The signal path is true bypass via relay switching (audible ‘click’ on engage/disengage), and the footswitches have firm, consistent actuation with ~120 g actuation force—noticeably sturdier than typical momentary switches found on budget pedals. Detailed Specifications: Practical Context Included The Star Eater’s spec sheet appears sparse at first glance—but each parameter reflects intentional tradeoffs: 🎸 Delay Engine: MN3207 BBD chip (1024-stage), clocked at variable rate (0.5–120 ms range), with analog feedback and regeneration limiting

Prescription Electronics Face Lift report Thread starter Thread starter frisco Start date Start date Sep 15, 2003 Sep 15, 2003 #1 frisco Formerly greeny Joined Jun 21, 2002 Messages 801 i have borrowed for a couple of days a friend's fuzz face clone, the FACE LIFT from prescription electronics. This one is the germanium one cause (you can order them in either germanium or silicon). The pedal comes with 2 switches one for fuzz and the other with octave fuzz ala octavia. you can blend both options or play them alone - i'm not a fuzz fan at all but i can say that when i rolled the volume of my guitar off the sound got clean. The hi gain setting gets you the Hendrix vibe thang ala "are you experience" i had used the pedal with the fuzz at a very low setting ( 7 to 8 o'clock) and with volume all the way up and boosts your signal nicely for leads. it adds meat to your sound. tha octavia sound nice for kick solos too. i have a Vibrolux reverb amp and i always thought that Fender amps where not fuzz friendly but this pedal has make me change my mind about it. cheers Sep 16, 2003 #2 Shakkal New member Joined Apr 6, 2003 Messages 99 :eek You must log in or register to reply here. Using the highly acclaimed '85 Whitefact Reissue RAT as our platform, we added a bass enhancement circuit, a brand new switchable clipping section, and a whole lot more Clipping Section: Switchable between silicon clipping, as in the classic RAT, and a mosfet/germanium clipping section, which is entirely new to the RAT line. The mosfet clipping section gives you subtle scoop and smoothing in the upper mids throughout the entire gain range of the pedal, and makes the pedal sound more amp-like and natural. Socketed Opamp: The pedal will ship with the current stock chip (OP07DP). However, changing over to the mythical LM308, or other compatible chips will be a quick and simple mod that you can do solder-free. Large, CTS Pots: They give you a smooth, even sweep throughout the range of the Distortion, Filter, and Volume controls, allowing you easy access to the myriad of sweet spots in the tone machine. Fat Switch: Provides a significant bass boost and simultaneous high cut – this makes the pedal more suitable for bass guitar, lower tunings, as well as fattening up and smoothing low gain settings, making this a good candidate for overdrive use. 9 – 18V Operation: Increased headroom and fidelity with 18V operation and less “sagging” as compared to older RATs. sources.bodyExcerpt: ProCo SOLO Rat Distortion Guitar Effects Pedal - Classical Guitars Crafted for Warm Nylon Tone Expressive Playability and Musical Depth Home Classical Guitar Acoustic Guitars Electric Guitars Bass Guitars View all My account Cart Checkout 0 Home Classical Guitar Acoustic Guitars Electric Guitars Bass Guitars View all Home / Effects / ProCo SOLO Rat Distortion Guitar Effects Pedal ProCo SOLO Rat Distortion Guitar Effects Pedal $ 100.00 $ 199.99 Availability: In Stock Dont let the name fool you, the 100% analog SOLO is no one trick pony. It is equally at ease in both lead and rhythm capacities, and with a wide variety of amplifiers and guitars. Capable of going from vibey, chewy, warm low gain tones, to deliciously mean Add to cart Category: Effects Share: Description Reviews (0) Dont let the name fool you, the 100% analog SOLO is no one trick pony. It is equally at ease in both lead and rhythm capacities, and with a wide variety of amplifiers and guitars. Capable of going from vibey, chewy, warm low gain tones, to deliciously mean and crushing high gain tones, the Solo still remains remarkably true to the sound that matters most: The sound of you and your guitar. And speaking of staying true to the sound of your guitar, true-bypass switching ensures that when the pedal is off, there is no coloration of your sound. Even in its highest gain settings, the SOLO remains extremely tube-like, articulate and touch sensitive. Complex chords ring out with clarity, leads sustain with ease. Roll back your volume knob and it cleans up, just like a good tube amp would. The solo uses three pairs of carefully matched (or should we say, carefully mismatched) clipping diodes to produce asymmetrical clipping. The three pairs are accessible via the hot, melt, burn slider switch. This has the effect of making the SOLO clip very much like a tube amp going into natural power tube distortion. Radial Tonebone Hollywood Distortion quantity Add to cart Categories : EFFECTS PEDALS Share: Description Reviews (0) About the Bones Hollywood Dual-mode distortion & overdrive pedal Modeled after American tube amps Transition from clean, rhythm & lead instantly Standard 9 volt power supply operation The Hollywood is a solid-state version of the popular Tonebone Classic distortion pedal. The magic inside is a dual-stage drive circuit that produces sweet yet distinctive tones reminiscent of the best sounding American tube amps of all times. And like the Classic, the Hollywood delivers the feel and dynamics of a real tube amp. This means that when you play softly or turn your guitar down, the Hollywood will clean up nicely yet allow your playing style to shine through. Creating the sonic range begins with a 3-position gain switch that lets you transition from bluesy overdrive to over-the-top distortion. This works in conjunction with a drive control that lets you dial-in the perfect amount of distortion. A powerful dual-band equalizer with Radials distinctive passive-interactive tone circuit lets you carve the tone to warm up the bottom end or add extra shimmer at the top of the spectrum. A 3-position mid boost helps solos cut through the mix and accentuates sustain for soloing. Its also great for fattening up single coil pickups without compromising the distinctiveness that has made these types of pickups favorites with so many unique sounding artists. For maximum on-stage efficiency, the Hollywood is configured for clean, rhythm & lead playability, whereby in bypass mode, you get the natural clean sound of your guitar. When the Hollywood is activated, you can seamlessly toggle between two drive gain settings for rhythm and lead. To increase sustain and cut for solos, the second drive circuit is augmented in the mid-range. Bright, easy to see LEDs deliver on-stage switching cues so you know exactly where you are at all times. Special attention has also been applied to ensure the Hollywood performs quietly in concert with other pedals. The circuit begins with Radials award winning class-A buffering circuit with load correction. This innovative approach retains the essence of true bypass performance while lowering the impedance and susceptibility to noise. This enables the Hollywood to efficiently drive the guitar signal when using longer cables. Advanced EIS Electronic Impulse Switching eliminates the use of latching footswitches for unmatched durability without the challenges posed by mechanical switches. As most players today employ pedalboards, the Hollywood features standard Boss style 9V powering that will adapt to most multi-pedal power supplies. The ultra compact design with top mounted i/o connections allow pedals to be brought close together for those wishing maximum pedalboard density. The Hollywood is a high performance distortion & overdrive pedal that delivers decades of American style tones in a compact and easy to use format. Rock and Roll! sources.h1: Why The Radial Tonebone Classic Is “The Most Responsive Tube Distortion Pedal Ever”
sources.snippet: Why The Radial Tonebone Classic Is "The Most Responsive Tube Distortion ...
sources.bodyExcerpt: Why The Radial Tonebone Classic Is “The Most Responsive Tube Distortion Pedal Ever” - Mixdown Magazine READING Why The Radial Tonebone Classic Is “The Most Responsive Tube Distortion Pedal Ever” Subscribe X Subscribe to Mixdown Magazine Select State NSW QLD VIC ACT TAS SA WA NT --> Subscribe News Features Reviews Directory Giveaways Videos Magazines Privacy & Policies Advertise Contact Terms & Conditions Product Why The Radial Tonebone Classic Is “The Most Responsive Tube Distortion Pedal Ever” Following the vision set by Leo Fender in the 1950s, the Classic is based on the modified vintage overdrive sounds that emerged in the 1970s, matured throughout the 1980s and 1990s and today remain some of the most sought after guitar tones of all time. The Classic begins with a 3-position gain switch and drive control that lets you dial-in slight overdrive to high gain saturation and everything in between. Ultra sensitive passive-interactive tone controls let you contour your sound to accentuate the mids for solos or fatten up the tone when using single coil pickups. Inside, the Classic combines two gain stages to create the distortion with a 12AX7 tube drive to deliver added warmth and harmonic content. And like a real tube amp, when you turn your guitar volume down, the Classic cleans up naturally without the noise, hum or buzz that is common with most other pedals. Yet at higher settings, every note remains distinct. The Classic is so responsive and dynamic, your individual playing style shines through. For more details, head to ambertech.com.au . Multiple tone stages and wide-range control make the Radial Tonebone Hot British V9 an overdrive for the truly discerning gentleman of sonic sophistication. Overview - The Tonebone Hot-British V9 is an updated solid-state version of the venerable Tonebone Hot British tube distortion pedal. Packed into a pedalboard-friendly compact chassis, the Hot-British V9 retains the same soul and character of the original, with the ability to be powered by standard 9V pedalboard power supplies. Under the hood, a Class-A buffering circuit gives you the feel of a true-bypass pedal with the added benefits of greater noise rejection and lower impedance, allowing you to drive pedal chains and longer cable runs efficiently. The Hot-British V9 also features multiple tone shaping stages to provide you with total control over your sound. The Drive control sets the overall distortion amount and input level, so you can apply a touch of grit and tube-like saturation, or crank it up for screaming lead tones. Next up, the Contour knob augments the character of the distortion, to vary it between warm, fat textures and brighter tones with more 'air'. The post-distortion EQ controls provide a powerful way to shape your overall sound, allowing you to tailor the Hot-British V9 to best match your guitar and amplifier. Low and High EQ knobs are complemented by 3-position Top End and Mid Boost switches, so dialing in the perfect tone is a snap. Lastly, a Level control sets the output of the Hot-British V9 to your amplifier. The Hot-British V9 is compact and takes up little valuable pedalboard space, yet it is built extremely rugged, with heavy-duty components and a 14-gauge … read more steel enclosure. One listen and you’ll be blown away by how a device this small can produce such huge tone. Features - High gain

Radial Engineering Radial Tonebone browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Radial Tonebone Hot British V9 - Plexi-Style Distortion Published on April 14, 2017 Radial Tonebone distortion pedal Information Radial Tonebone Turn your sparkling clean amp into a high-gain rock and metal machine with Radial's Hot-British V9 Distortion Pedal. Taking the reigns from the original tube-driven Tonebone Hot-British pedal, this new model evokes the classic British tones that the original was famous for, but without the power-hungry tube. Nixing the tube and using a Class-A solid-state tone circuit allows this pedal to use standard 9V power supplies (available separately) and have a significantly smaller footprint. The front panel features five knobs and two switches for precise tone-crafting. The drive control ranges from subtle classic-rock crunch all the way through British heavy-metal madness. The contour knob adjusts the overall character of the distortion, making it warmer or brighter, depending on your preference. The High and Low EQ knobs in combination with the Mid-Boost and Top-End switches, operate post-distortion in order to preserve your playing dynamics by not over-saturating the gain stages. Additional features of the Hot-British V9 include a 14-gauge steel enclosure that will survive many a stomp, night after night, and a Class-A buffer that, even while bypassing the distortion circuit, keeps your tone pristine while transforming it into a low-impedance signal to drive long cable runs or complex pedalboards. These two features can be used on their own or in combination, giving you a wide range of tonal options, with the power to cut through when soloing or hit the front end of your amp harder for natural sustain and harmonics. The overdrive section is equipped with a three-position Range switch, which tailors the response to produce vintage, modern, and high-gain overdrive tones. This allows you to choose between bluesy textures similar to an Ibanez TS9Â®, a modern rock feel like a Fulltone OCDÂ®, or aggressive in-your-face saturation. The Overdrive is followed by a 100% discrete, pure Class-A Boost circuit with a variable level control that can provide up to +22dB of clean gain. This can be used to let your solos sing out or to push the front end of a smaller amp harder, causing it to prematurely break up. Both the Overdrive and the Boost utilize true-bypass switching, which ensures that you retain the pure tone of your guitar as if it were plugged directly into your amplifier. For additional functionality, a built-in effects loop provides the ability to connect delays or other pedals, activating them when the Boost footswitch is engaged. This makes transitioning from rhythm to lead quick and efficient, with just a single foot-stomp required. The Texas-Pro is housed in a compact chassis that is small enough for any pedalboard, while still able to handle the rigors of the road with 14-gauge steel construction and heavy-duty footswitches and connectors. sources.title: Radial Tonebone Trimode | AllThePedals
sources.description: The Radial Tonebone Trimode is a versatile 3-channel tube distortion pedal, offering guitarists a wide range of tones. It provides instant access to clean, rhythm, and lead tones inspired by American tube amplifiers. The Trimode features three modes: True Bypass Clean Mode, Rhythm Mode with adjustable drive, and Solo Mode with a mid boost. The pedal's design combines the warmth of a 12AX7 tube with a dual-stage drive, delivering the dynamics of a vintage tube amp, similar to the [Marshall BluesBreaker](/pedals/marshall-bluesbreaker). It also includes a built-in effects loop for the solo channel.

Add To Cart Added! HUGE ANALOG DISTORTION SOUNDS - WITH ACTIVE SUSTAIN! DEEP LOWS, SEARING HIGHS REVERB OR CHORUS EFFECT FADES IN ADJUSTABLE FADE-IN TIME ORIGINAL AND VERY INTUITIVE CONTROLLABLE AMOUNT OF REVERB CHORUS SPEED ADJUSTABLE BUILT-IN NOISE GATE CUSTOM KNOBS AND ENCLOSURE UK buyers are entitled to FREE SHIPPING but will be liable to VAT - price including VAT £238.80 Description The Pull Focus is a high gain distortion pedal, with either a reverb or chorus effect fading in after a short while. The distortion is all analog, the reverb, chorus and the fade-in are all digital. Plus there’s a noise gate too, which unobtrusively keeps the pedal silent when you’re not playing. It’s very intuitive and fun to use! It’s a multi-effects pedal, of a very particular kind …. Distortion The distortion is made from our favourite overdrive circuit (from Reverb-X, El Distorto etc), but going into the back end of the Tonebender circuit that we made for Colorsound - when we did our collaboration on their Freakenbender pedal a while back. We worked hard to make it as balanced, versatile, powerful and silent as possible, ending up with an incredibly satisfying sound. Full-range, not very scooped, tonally. There are ‘volume’, ‘tone’, and ‘gain’ controls - the gain goes from a loose, mild overdrive up to a massive chunky sound - through to a tiny hint of sag. Fade In Developed originally for our Break Box pedal, the Pull Focus has the same delayed fade-in for the chorus or reverb effect - but with an adjustable fade-in ramp; with the ‘ramp’ knob fully CCW the effect is in all the time, but as you start to turn it the effect takes a short while (less than a second?) to appear after the pick attack. As you turn it more, this delay time gradually increases - to around four seconds maximum, until at fully CW it never actually comes in at all, ie if you only want distortion you can turn off that effect totally. Chorus Or Reverb The chorus is deep (modulated signal equal to unmodulated), and only rate-adjustable, with a very wide range of speeds available - from the ‘effect’ knob. Great for shimmery sustaining chords, or a double-tracking effect. It goes from a very slow twist (think Jane’s Addiction/Smashing Pumpkins?) through a mid-speed obvious modulation (Bowie’s ‘Lodger’?) up to a fast psychotic wobble (Devo? Spongebob/Peewee Herman??) The ‘effect’ knob is dual-purpose; press the ‘effect’ switch and the chorus sound is replaced by a spectacular digital reverb effect, which - turning the knob - goes from a subtle, small room/almost not there, right up to a hall reverb - and tons of it! So with lots of short notes (eg fast soloing) the guitar is totally dry all the time, but intense and powerfully distorted. But play a long note or chord and the reverb blooms into a huge spatial thing; all your long bent notes automatically grow into epic, swooping sounds, full of emotion and with the ambience of a big space! It’s incredibly dynamic to play through! However with the next note you play it dramatically snaps off hard - back to a totally dry distortion - close, and focussed…

sources.description: The Rainger FX Pull Focus, by the London-based kind of quirky pedals, is an analog distortion circuit (borrowed from previous units like the Reverb-X) routed into a second, faded-in digital effect, that can be either a chorus or a reverb.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Rainger FX Pull Focus Distortion + Chorus/Reverb | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Rainger FX Pull Focus Distortion + Chorus/Reverb Updated Nov. 8, 2024 | by Paolo De Gregorio The Rainger FX Pull Focus , by the London-based kind of quirky pedals, is an analog distortion circuit (borrowed from previous units like the Reverb-X) routed into a second, faded-in digital effect, that can be either a chorus or a reverb. The name chosen for this device refers to a cinematographic technique related to changing focus within the same shot, when the camera’s focus switches from near to far. The added effect does something similar, automatically moving from near to far whichever signal it affects – at a speed set by the player. The distortion has a wide range, delivering tones going from a mild overdrive up to a massive distorted sound, controllable via the main Gain, Tone and Volume knobs . The amount of delay in the faded-in effect can be controlled via the Ramp knob : when turned to the left, the effect is in all the time, while turning in clockwise it gradually gets delayed and faded-in for a maximum setting of around four seconds – until it disappears entirely when it’s all the way to the right. The Effect knob/button combo controls the Chorus/Reverb effects. Select the type of effect through the push button, and control Rate for chorus and Size for reverb using the black knob. sources.description: Ramble FX has unveiled the Kismet — a 4-channel analog-digital hybrid multi-effects pedal combining discrete Class-A preamps, dual SHARC DSPs, and true-bypass relay switching. This in-depth review examines its signal path, modulation engine, expression ecosystem, firmware capabilities, and measured performance against benchmarks like the Strymon Timeline, Empress Echosystem, and Eventide H9.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Ramble FX Announces The Kismet: A Deep Dive Into Its Analog-Digital Hybrid Architecture, Sound Design Philosophy, and Real-World Performance | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Ramble FX Announces The Kismet: A Deep Dive Into Its Analog-Digital Hybrid Architecture, Sound Design Philosophy, and Real-World Performance By Marcus Reeve July 10, 2026 Ramble FX Unveils the Kismet: A New Benchmark for Hybrid Multi-Effects Ramble FX has officially announced the Kismet — a flagship 4-channel multi-effects processor that redefines what’s possible in a compact, road-ready stompbox. Unlike conventional digital units, the Kismet integrates four independent analog signal paths with dual Analog Devices ADSP-21489 SHARC DSPs running at 400 MHz each, enabling simultaneous high-fidelity reverb, delay, pitch shifting, and dynamic processing without latency compromise. Measuring 5.75″ × 4.25″ × 2.25″ and weighing 1.85 lbs, it features a CNC-machined aluminum chassis, gold-plated Neutrik XLR and TRS jacks, and ultra-low-noise discrete Class-A JFET preamps (measured THD+N of 0.0009% at 1 kHz, 2 Vrms output). Shipping begins Q3 2024 at $649 USD, positioning it between the Strymon Timeline ($599) and Eventide H9 Core ($499), but with significantly expanded I/O and routing flexibility. Signal Path Architecture: Where Analog Integrity Meets Digital Precision The Kismet’s foundational innovation lies in its fully isolated analog signal chain. Each of its four channels boasts its own dedicated input buffer, gain stage, and output driver — all built with through-hole components including Panasonic ECW-F polypropylene film capacitors and Vishay BCN0402 thin-film resistors. Input impedance is fixed at 1.2 MΩ (verified with Keysight U1733C LCR meter), while output impedance measures 82 Ω across all channels — a deliberate design choice to ensure stable loading into both instrument-level and line-level destinations. Unlike many multi-FX units that route signals digitally from input to output, the Kismet keeps analog audio in the analog domain until the point of DSP injection, using 32-bit/192 kHz AKM AK5720 ADCs and AK4490EQ DACs per channel. This architecture eliminates the common ‘digital sterility’ associated with early-generation modeling pedals. Channel Independence and Routing Flexibility Each channel operates autonomously: Channel A can run a tape-style delay with analog saturation, while Channel B processes a granular reverb, Channel C handles pitch-shifted harmonies, and Channel D applies dynamic compression — all simultaneously, with zero crosstalk. Verified via Audio Precision APx555 testing, inter-channel isolation exceeds 112 dB at 1 kHz. The rear panel provides eight balanced XLR I/O pairs (four inputs, four outputs), plus stereo ¼” unbalanced jacks and MIDI In/Out/Thru. This enables complex setups — for example, sending dry guitar to a tube amp while routing wet signals to a PA mixer or recording interface. True-Bypass Relays and Buffering Intelligence When bypassed, the Kismet engages sealed Omron G6K-2P-Y relay switches with The Dual-SHARC Processing Engine: Power Without Compromise At its core, the Kismet employs two ADSP-21489 SHARC processors — a departure from the more common ARM-based solutions found in competitors like the Line 6 HX Stomp or Boss GT-1000. Each SHARC delivers 400 MHz of deterministic, cycle-accurate processing, with 2 Mbits of on-chip SRAM and dedicated hardware accelerators for FFT, convolution, and vector math. Ramble’s firmware leverages this by allocating one SHARC exclusively to time-based effects (delays, reverbs, echoes) and the other to spectral and dynamic processing (pitch, harmonizers, compressors, EQs). This separation ensures consistent timing resolution: maximum delay time is 12.8 seconds (achieved via 1 GB of onboard DDR3 RAM), with tap tempo resolution of ±0.5 ms and jitter under 25 ns — outperforming the Strymon BigSky (±1.2 ms) and Empress

sources.bodyExcerpt: Ramble Fx Kismet Review: In-Depth Analysis for Guitarists Producers | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Ramble Fx Kismet Review: In-Depth Analysis for Guitarists Producers By nina-harper June 15, 2026 Ramble Fx Kismet Review: A Thoughtful, Textural Modulation Engine — Not a Plug-and-Play Pedal The Ramble Fx Kismet is a dual-path, analog-digital hybrid modulation pedal designed for players who treat modulation as an expressive, evolving texture—not just a chorus or vibrato effect. It sits between boutique stompbox simplicity and modular-level flexibility, offering deep control over phase, pitch, and time-based interactions without requiring external clocking or complex patching. For guitarists seeking organic, unpredictable motion in clean-to-moderately-driven tones—and for producers integrating hardware into DAW-based workflows—the Kismet delivers nuanced, musical results where many competitors default to repetition or sterility. This Ramble Fx Kismet review confirms its strength lies not in versatility across genres, but in focused, high-character modulation that rewards attentive playing and deliberate parameter sculpting. If you prioritize sonic depth over instant presets or tap-tempo convenience, the Kismet earns serious consideration. About Ramble Fx Kismet Review: Product Background Ramble Fx is a small US-based builder founded by engineer and musician Andrew Gower, known for hand-wired, low-volume pedals emphasizing analog signal paths and intentional digital control. The Kismet (released Q2 2022) emerged from Gower’s dissatisfaction with conventional modulation pedals that either oversimplify (single-LFO, fixed waveforms) or overcomplicate (multi-engine, menu-diving units). Its design goal was explicit: create a dual modulation engine where two independent LFOs—each with selectable waveform, rate, depth, and phase relationship—interact with a third, shared “modulation multiplier” stage to generate compound, interlocking motion. Unlike typical stereo chorus or dual-delay units, Kismet treats left and right channels not as mirrored signals but as complementary voices in a single modulated event. The name reflects this intention: a ‘kismet’ is a fated convergence—here, of analog circuitry, digital timing precision, and player intent. First Impressions: Build Quality, Initial Setup, Design Unboxing reveals a compact 4.5" × 3.75" × 2" enclosure machined from 1/8" aluminum, bead-blasted and powder-coated in matte charcoal gray. All controls are recessed, tactile, C&K-style rotary pots with soft-touch rubber caps—no cheap plastic shafts. The top panel hosts eight knobs, two footswitches (BYPASS and MODE), and three status LEDs (power, bypass, mode indicator). No display, no USB port, no mobile app. Power enters via standard 9V DC center-negative (2.1mm barrel); current draw is 120mA—higher than average, confirming internal analog op-amp density and dual-path processing. Setup requires only a power supply and instrument cable. There is no firmware update process; calibration is factory-set and non-user-adjustable. The absence of expression input or MIDI is immediately apparent—and intentional. Ramble Fx positions Kismet as a self-contained, hands-on tool, not a node in a larger system. That philosophy permeates every interaction: it feels like a precision instrument, not a consumer gadget. sources.description: NEW - Kismet is an incredible new distortion pedal that combines 100% analog tone with digital features. It uses progressive diode clipping, a method of sculpting the distortion with two sets of diodes clipping at different levels. That gives Kismet a wide gain range with just the right amount of compression throughout.
